video.title: 10 Simple Businesses You Can Start This Weekend

summary: Tim Richard lists 10 low-cost local service businesses that can be started over a weekend: dog poop scooping, fence staining, photo organizing, garage cleaning, senior companion care, graffiti removal, cardboard recycling pickup, gutter cleaning, mattress and couch cleaning, and parking lot cleaning. Most examples are second-hand anecdotes with large income claims. The main marketing tactic is a personalised flyer with the owner's face and a written price for that specific property, plus local Facebook community posts. The video also promotes the host's paid 'idea book' database.

speakers.name: Tim Richard
speakers.description: YouTuber who researches low-competition local service business ideas and sells an 'idea book' database.

ideas.name: Dog poop scooping service
ideas.one_liner: Weekly or fortnightly subscription pet waste removal for homeowners.
ideas.problem: Owners dislike picking up dog waste from their yard.

acquisition_channels.details: Took donuts and flyers to doggy daycares and vet centres and asked to leave flyers on the counter.

quote.text: she actually took a box of donuts around to doggy daycares, veterinarian centers, brought the donuts in with a stack of her flyers
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

acquisition_channels.details: Put flyers on people's doorsteps.
Posted on local Facebook community pages.

ideas.delivery: Owner physically visits yards on a recurring route.
unit_economics_claims: Erica Krupin reportedly reached $100,000 in the first year, working alone.

acquisition.how: Flyers and in-person drops are physical; Facebook posts can be partly drafted by agents but are manual.

onboarding.how: Booking forms and scheduling can be automated.

support.how: Agents can handle scheduling and rescheduling queries.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK. Flyering is legal; Facebook group posts need group rules checked; pricing in GBP.

risks: Physical work caps scale at the owner's time

quotes.text: within the first year she was doing $100,000 by herself
quotes.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.name: Fence painting and staining
ideas.one_liner: Stain or seal fences, sold via personalised priced flyers.
ideas.problem: Fences need re-staining or sealing and owners don't want to do it.
ideas.offer: Fence, deck and pergola staining at a fixed quoted price

pricing.notes: Host's example price written on the flyer.

acquisition_channels.details: Flyer with logo, host's face photo and services, blank lines for a handwritten price; walk the neighbourhood, estimate each fence, write a price and a note, leave it on the door, customer texts to book.

quote.text: That personalized touch of your picture and a written note with an exact price that you offer converts really well.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

unit_economics_claims: Average ticket for an average fence about $800.

acquisition.how: Walking the neighbourhood and leaving handwritten flyers is in-person work.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK; fence panels are common, but weather limits the season. Personal data on flyers is fine, but unsolicited leaflets should respect 'no junk mail' signs.

quotes.text: The average ticket for this for an average size fence is between $800
quotes.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.name: Photo organizing service
ideas.one_liner: Organise people's phone photo libraries for a fee.
ideas.customer: People with thousands of unsorted phone photos
ideas.problem: Photos pile up and are never looked at.

pricing.notes: She raised prices as demand grew; none stated.

acquisition_channels.details: Organised own photos, then friends', then posted on the local Facebook community page; word of mouth followed.

quote.text: she posted on her local Facebook community page, and before she knew it, she had more people asking her to organize their photos than she could handle
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

acquisition_channels.details: Word spread from friends.

ideas.delivery: Done on the customer's photos, largely digital work by one person.
unit_economics_claims: A Chicago mom reportedly makes $20,000 per month.

acquisition.how: Community posts and content are largely automatable.

delivery.how: AI tagging and dedupe tools can do much of it; the customer's taste needs review.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK. Handling private photos needs UK GDPR care and trust.

risks: Privacy and trust with personal photos

quotes.text: One mom in Chicago is making $20,000 a month just organizing people's photos.
quotes.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.name: Garage organizing and cleaning
ideas.one_liner: Clean out and organise homeowners' garages.
ideas.problem: Garages become cluttered and owners lack time or will to clear them.

pricing.notes: Host says customers didn't blink at the price.

acquisition_channels.details: Handed out flyers.
Posted on the local Facebook community page.
Word of mouth spread; no website or Google listing.

quote.text: He didn't even really have a website or a Google business listing.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.delivery: Owner does the labour on site.
unit_economics_claims: Reportedly $60,000 in 3 months at about $600 per garage.
Described as mostly profit since it is only labour.

acquisition.how: Facebook and flyer content can be agent-drafted, but flyering is manual.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK, but waste disposal needs a waste carrier licence and tip fees.

risks: Waste disposal legality in the UK

quotes.text: the guy doing this made $60,000 in just 3 months. He charges on average $600 per garage
quotes.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.name: Senior companion care
ideas.one_liner: Paid non-medical companionship for elderly people living alone.
ideas.business_model: Recurring contract per hour or visit
ideas.customer: Adult children of elderly parents living alone
ideas.problem: Families can't always be there for ageing parents.
ideas.offer: Conversation, card games, grocery trips, mail sorting

acquisition_channels.details: Post on the local Facebook community page.
Flyers at libraries and where adult children go.

ideas.delivery: Companion visits in person; can scale by hiring multiple companions.
unit_economics_claims: Some reportedly make over $10,000 per month as full-time companions.

acquisition.how: Facebook posts and local content are partly automatable; flyers are manual.

onboarding.how: Intake and vetting still need human conversation.

uk_applicability.notes: Non-personal-care companionship is not CQC-regulated in England, but DBS checks, insurance and safeguarding are expected; the host's no-training claim is US-based.

quotes.text: there are people making over $10,000 a month being senior companions
quotes.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.name: Graffiti removal
ideas.one_liner: Remove graffiti from commercial and city buildings with a pressure washer and chemicals.
ideas.customer: Commercial building owners and city governments
ideas.offer: Graffiti removal at a quoted price

acquisition_channels.details: Drive around spotting graffiti, walk into the business and quote, then leave a card for repeat work.

quote.text: I would drive around town and look for graffiti. I would mainly look for graffiti on commercial buildings.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

acquisition_channels.details: Call city authorities and offer removal across the city.

ideas.delivery: Pressure washing and chemicals on site.

acquisition.how: Spotting and walk-ins are in person; council outreach by email can be automated.

uk_applicability.notes: Works with changes: councils often run their own removal, and removing graffiti on private property needs owner consent; pricing in GBP.

ideas.name: Cardboard recycling pickup subscription
ideas.one_liner: Weekly subscription to collect and optionally break down household cardboard.
ideas.customer: Households with piles of online-order cardboard
ideas.problem: Cardboard piles up and doesn't fit in small recycling bins.
ideas.offer: Weekly cardboard pickup, with a cheaper tier if already broken down

acquisition_channels.details: Post on the local community page.
Hand out flyers and post one at the recycling drop-off centre.

ideas.delivery: Weekly route; cardboard dropped off free at the recycling centre.
unit_economics_claims: Cardboard disposal free, so cost is mainly gas and time.

acquisition.how: Community posts are automatable; flyers are manual.

uk_applicability.notes: UK councils already collect cardboard, and commercial waste carriers need a licence. Demand may be weaker and a waste carrier registration may be required.

risks: Low willingness to pay given council collections
Waste carrier licensing in the UK

quotes.text: the cool thing about cardboard is you can get rid of it for free
quotes.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.name: Gutter cleaning
ideas.one_liner: Clean gutters with basic tools using personalised priced flyers.
ideas.problem: Gutters clog and owners avoid climbing ladders.
ideas.offer: Gutter cleaning at a quoted price

acquisition_channels.details: Same personalised flyer with face, service and a handwritten price on each house; text to book.

quote.text: A flyer with your face on it, your service, and then some lines down below where you can walk around, look at someone's gutters
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.delivery: Ladder, gloves and bag, done by the owner.
unit_economics_claims: Six figures a year reportedly possible, per YouTuber Mike Check.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK; consider insurance and working-at-height safety.

quotes.text: how people are making six figures a year cleaning gutters
quotes.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.name: Mattress and couch cleaning
ideas.one_liner: Clean mattresses, couches and carpets with a machine, ranking locally for low-competition keywords.
ideas.customer: Homeowners with multiple mattresses and couches

pricing.notes: Host says a couple of mattresses and couches could be hundreds of dollars.

acquisition_channels.details: Long term, build a website targeting couch cleaning and sofa cleaning keywords.
Post on the local community page.
Flyers with face, exact pricing and a phone number to text.

ideas.delivery: On-site cleaning with a bought or rented machine.
unit_economics_claims: Equipment is a couple of hundred dollars.

acquisition.how: Local SEO is automatable; flyers are optional.

uk_applicability.notes: Works the same in the UK; local search demand exists and machine hire is available.

quotes.text: a simple couple hundred dollar item could get you up and running this weekend
quotes.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.name: Commercial parking lot cleaning
ideas.one_liner: Recurring after-hours clean-up of medium strip-mall parking lots.
ideas.customer: Owners of medium strip malls with 5-10 businesses
ideas.problem: Lots need regular litter, debris and weed clearing.

acquisition_channels.details: Call as many property owners as possible; described as a numbers game.

quote.text: it's a numbers game, so just calling on as many as you can, telling them what you offer
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

ideas.delivery: Cleaning at night with simple tools, started while working full-time.
unit_economics_claims: Brian reportedly made $650,000 profit per year.

acquisition.how: B2B outreach to companies can be automated; calls need TPS/CTPS screening, and email to limited companies is lawful.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK for retail parks and shopping parades; facilities firms are common competitors.

tactics.name: Personalised priced flyer
steps: Make a flyer with a simple logo, your face photo and the services offered.
Leave blank lines at the bottom.
Walk the neighbourhood, assess each fence, deck or gutter, and write a specific price and a short note.
Put it on the front door and invite the customer to text you to book for the weekend.

quote.text: I would write there, "Hey, my name's Tim. I was looking at your fence. I could restain it for you for $500.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

tactics.name: Leave flyers at pet businesses
steps: Bring a box of donuts and a stack of flyers to doggy daycares and vet centres.
Ask to leave flyers on the counter, where every visitor has a pet.

tactics.name: Walk-in quote for visible problems
steps: Drive around and spot graffiti on commercial buildings.
Walk in and offer removal at a set price, e.g. $200.
Leave a card for future incidents.
Also offer the city a standing arrangement.

tactics.name: Grow organically from own and friends' work
steps: Start by doing the service on your own items.
Do it for a few friends.
Post on the local Facebook community page.
Raise prices as demand exceeds capacity.

tactics.name: Target mid-sized commercial properties
steps: Choose medium strip malls with 5-10 businesses, not too small or too large.
Work after hours alongside a day job.

warnings.warning: Starting one of these businesses doesn't guarantee income or the results of the examples; do your own research.

quote.text: just cuz you start one of these doesn't mean you're going to automatically make money.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: A personalised, priced offer for a specific visible job (a named price for this fence or gutter) lowers friction compared with a generic flyer.

quote.text: I think this works very well for anything you can see outside someone's home and write down a price.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: Recurring-service models (weekly pickup, scooping, parking lots) need fewer customers to reach solid revenue.

quote.text: Since it is recurring revenue, you wouldn't need that many customers to really start making some solid revenue
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: Boring, low-skill local services with low competition can be started with minimal capital.
Selling to commercial property owners and working off-hours allows starting alongside a full-time job.
Low-competition local keywords like couch cleaning give a long-term SEO route after initial grassroots outreach.
Raise prices when demand exceeds capacity, as the photo organiser did.
Most income figures here are second-hand anecdotes and should be validated locally before relying on them.

evidence_quality.rationale: Listicle of second-hand anecdotes with unverified income figures, no first-hand operator detail, and very few concrete prices or costs.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host sells the 'idea book' database of business ideas and promotes it in the video.
